clue.text: The brains of the Lady Jane affair?

definitions.text: The brains of the Lady Jane affair?

parts.words: The brains of the Lady Jane affair?
parts.note: Lady Jane Grey was the nine-day Tudor queen; the stuff of the brain is named as if it were her business

explanation.surface: A question about who masterminded the plot surrounding Lady Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Jane Grey was proclaimed Queen of England in 1553 and reigned nine days; 'affair' is taken as 'matter', so a Grey matter is the brain's tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebral tissue of the brain is commonly called by this name, and by extension intelligence itself.

clue.text: Highlander has the wind up, we hear

indicators.note: this signals that the word is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: a gale is wind that has got up strongly

explanation.surface: A Scottish Highlander is frightened, so people report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has the wind up' means is scared in the surface; here it supplies a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gael is a Gaelic-speaking Celt of the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Take out a bit more-cut the centre out

parts.note: something extra is a bit more

indicators.note: the middle letter of the three-letter word is removed

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove a little more, trimming out the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the centre out' drops the U from CUT to leave CT.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw or pull something out.

clue.text: Do they help Masons to get college caps?

definitions.meaning: boards holding mortar used by stonemasons and bricklayers
flat square academic hats worn at universities

explanation.surface: Asking whether Freemasons help each other into university caps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masons' with a capital suggests Freemasons; it is builders who use hawk boards for mortar.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the plasterer's hawk and the square academic cap are called by this name.

clue.text: Trod on hobo who was in the van

parts.note: a hobo is a tramp, a vagrant
to be in the vanguard, at the front, is to have led

explanation.surface: A vagrant who rode in a van was stepped on.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread heavily on something.

clue.text: Hemingway's " The Way of an Eagle "'?

definitions.note: the possessive points to the novelist's first name

indicators.note: a way of an eagle is one belonging to it, so the way's letters follow the bird's

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A title of a supposed Hemingway book about an eagle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Way of an Eagle was really a 1912 novel by Ethel M Dell, not by Hemingway; the quotation marks disguise the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist Hemingway's first name was Ernest.

clue.text: Powerful. network put on the map

definitions.meaning: the national electricity network that carries power across the country
the squared lattice of reference lines printed over a map

explanation.surface: A strong network of contacts gets a place noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the power-supply system and the map's lattice of numbered squares share this name.

clue.text: Makes sharp reply about damaging offences

parts.note: re means about, concerning
torts are civil wrongs causing harm

explanation.surface: Someone snaps back about harmful misdeeds.
explanation.definitionFit: To retort is to answer back sharply or wittily.

clue.text: Editor has posy made up for 27

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 27 across, a warehouse

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new form

explanation.surface: An editor makes a little bouquet for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made up' rearranges EDITOR and POSY; 27 across is STOREHOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A depository is a place where things are deposited for safekeeping, a warehouse.

clue.text: Cherishes an interest in variety

indicators.note: variety means a mixed assortment, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone keeps up a fond interest in music-hall variety shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in variety' tells you to jumble AN INTEREST into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour or hold an idea or hope in mind is to cherish it.

clue.text: Short way to record measure

parts.note: ST is the abbreviated form of street, a way
an EP is an extended-play gramophone record

explanation.surface: Advice on a quick way to measure for a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A step is a measured stride, and also a course of action, a measure taken.

clue.text: Tom Thumb's breeches?

parts.note: the tiny folk-tale hero's trousers would be very little garments

explanation.surface: Asking about the trousers of the tiny folk hero.
explanation.walkthrough: The old term for knee-breeches is read literally as tiny clothes fit for Tom Thumb, the thumb-sized hero of English folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallclothes was an eighteenth-century term for knee-breeches.

clue.text: Art-school gets positive responses from Moscow

parts.note: da is Russian for yes, so two of them are a pair of yeses
da is Russian for yes; the plural asks for a second one

explanation.surface: An art college receives favourable replies from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: Dada was the early twentieth-century anti-art movement; 'school' here is a movement in art, not a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Dada was a movement in early twentieth-century art, a school of artists in that sense.

clue.text: Hand over money for success in Test ?

parts.note: to pass something is to hand it over
marks were the German currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Bribing someone to get through an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Grades high enough to clear an examination count as getting through it.

clue.text: One can claim credit for being here

definitions.text: One can claim credit for being here

parts.words: One can claim credit for being here
parts.note: a bank account in credit, with figures once written in dark ink, not red

explanation.surface: Someone takes credit simply for turning up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claim credit' reads as taking praise; it means having a positive balance, solvent rather than in the red.
explanation.definitionFit: Being solvent with money in the account is described by this phrase.

clue.text: Eminent incompetents?

parts.note: important people, playfully split as those who are not able

explanation.surface: A jibe at distinguished people who are useless at their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as NOT ABLES and it describes incompetents; as one word it means eminent people.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguished and prominent persons are called by this name.

clue.text: A little room near a sort of square

parts.note: close means near
a T-square is a drawing instrument shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: Describing a small room next to some kind of town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard or small private chamber is called a closet.

clue.text: A jam ? Keep going

definitions.meaning: a conserve of fruit cooked with sugar
to maintain or keep something in existence

explanation.surface: Stuck in a traffic jam, someone urges keeping going.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit conserve and the act of keeping something intact share this word.

clue.text: Inn-keeper as producer of flowers

definitions.note: the clue is singular for a plural answer: these garden plants each produce flowers

parts.note: a landlord who keeps an inn is the host

explanation.surface: A landlord who also grows flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostas are leafy garden perennials that send up spikes of lilac or white blooms.

clue.text: Church's custodian of 101 stars, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged otherwise

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A church keeper in charge of a hundred and one stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrist is the officer who looks after a church's sacred vessels and vestments, a sacristan.

clue.text: Critical situation for the amateur

parts.note: the seat from which a non-expert criticises, as in the phrase for an amateur critic

explanation.surface: Seemingly a crisis facing a non-professional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Critical situation' suggests a crisis; it is where the armchair critic sits passing judgement without taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic judges from comfort without practical experience, so the comfy seat is the amateur's critical position.

clue.text: Shock with regard to a French note

parts.note: as to means concerning
un is French for a
D is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Being shocked about a French musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or stun.

clue.text: A score-draw you say ? How exquisite !

indicators.note: you say signals the words are said aloud

parts.note: a football match ending two-all is a score draw

explanation.surface: A football fan hears of a draw and gushes about it.
explanation.walkthrough: A score draw is a drawn football match with goals, as in the pools; two-two is the classic one.
explanation.definitionFit: Too-too is an affected exclamation meaning excessively refined or precious.

clue.text: Reverse rod, so changing means of access

parts.note: to back is to reverse, as a car

indicators.note: the letters of the two short words are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Instructions to turn a rod round and so alter how one gets in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' scrambles ROD and SO into DOORS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rear entrances, and figuratively indirect routes, are ways of getting in.

clue.text: Chooses to remove head of Egyptian sectaries

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is dropped here

parts.note: the Copts are the Christians of the ancient Egyptian church

explanation.surface: Someone decides to behead members of an Egyptian sect.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a choice, so this means picks.

clue.text: Divine power causes canal to rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and Red Sea

explanation.surface: A god makes a canal's water level go up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns SUEZ upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeus was the supreme deity of the Greek pantheon.

clue.text: Bill I had for LSD

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Admitting to having been charged for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is the slang name for the hallucinogenic drug lysergic acid diethylamide.

clue.text: Keeper's lodge?

parts.note: a building where goods are kept, as though a gamekeeper's cottage

explanation.surface: Asking about the cottage of a gamekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: A keeper's lodge suggests a gamekeeper's home; it is a building where things are kept, a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A warehouse or depot where goods are stored is a building for keeping things.

clue.text: Bird used on test-flight

definitions.meaning: a fork-tailed bird of prey of the hawk family
to fly one is to float an idea to test opinion

explanation.surface: A bird used to try out a new aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the raptor and the trial balloon of opinion share this name, from flying a paper toy.

clue.text: Serious sort of teams, avoiding tight corners?

definitions.meaning: sides, or teams, that keep from getting tight, that is drunk

explanation.surface: Describing earnest teams who steer clear of awkward spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight corners' suggests difficulties, but 'tight' means drunk: teams avoiding it are sober sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A staid, earnest person is jokingly called by this name.
